commits.message:
[iris] Test proxy response routing under concurrency (#9492)

Replace the proxy test's upstream TCP connection count with response
checks for sequential and concurrent requests. The old assertion fails
on clean main after every request succeeds. Distinct request paths now
verify that each response reaches the correct caller without
constraining connection pooling.

The affected safe suite passes (13 tests). All-files lint, Pyrefly, and
advisory lint review pass.

Part of #9487

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris] Share uv cache files on TPU worker hosts (#9489)

Use symlinks for Iris-managed uv installs on TPU worker hosts, including
CPU tasks placed there. On the reported GCP v4 hosts, copied
environments added about 6.5 GB per task; disk exhaustion caused
worker-health failures and controller removal on 215 GB hosts.
Kubernetes keeps copy mode because its node agent may clean the shared
uv cache while tasks run, which would break symlinked environments.

A test with a local wheel verifies cache-backed symlinks and copy-mode
imports after cache deletion. The affected safe suite (`uv run
--no-project infra/ci/run_tests.py`) passed 4,846 tests and failed
`test_native_proxy_reuses_upstream_connections`; the Iris CI unit job
failed the same test. It also fails in isolation on a clean main
checkout at `3a4e6506d4`, opening 16 upstream connections for 16
sequential requests where the test expects one. The [incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/540) has the production
measurements. A live post-deploy disk measurement remains outstanding.

Fixes #9487

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Route Evalchemy locally and reuse proxy connections (#9480)

On the serving Iris cluster, Evalchemy resolves each vLLM endpoint
through Iris's endpoint API before an evaluation and sends requests to
its in-cluster address, bypassing the public capability proxy. Harbor's
external Daytona sandboxes keep capability URLs for candidate and hosted
judge endpoints. The orchestrator scrapes vLLM metrics directly. The
Rust proxy retains up to 256 idle upstream connections per host and
closes them after 90 seconds idle.

During five minutes of September 26 eval load, Finelog recorded 7,734
additional hub proxy 502s and 10,749 additional CoreWeave peer proxy
502s. An affected JSON response said `upstream transport error: client
error (Connect)`, identifying the Rust proxy's upstream request path.
Its upstream pool retained zero idle connections, forcing a new
connection after every completed request. Connection churn is a
plausible contributor; the historical response does not expose the
socket error. In a later run, a serving task was preempted at 20:20:29
UTC. The proxy returned `No endpoint` 404s after its 10-minute
registration lease expired and until a replacement registered at
20:35:07. No ready endpoint was registered during that interval.
[Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/529).

[PR #9484](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9484) preserves
Evalchemy transport failures in records and gates low-coverage runs. The
Rust proxy change requires an updated Iris controller image on the hub
and `cw-rno2a` peer.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[serve] Forward backend tokenization requests (#9482)

Forward `/tokenize` through the serving proxy. Harbor uses this endpoint
to
count context tokens; the missing route returned HTTP 404 and forced its
fallback token counter during agentic evaluations. See the incident:
https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/532

The proxy forwards request bodies unchanged and preserves the backend's
HTTP
status and response body. Existing serving jobs must be relaunched with
this
change to expose the route; Harbor's tokenization payload is unchanged.
